newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo end mixed, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo end mixed, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Wednesday, with major investors staying on the sidelines waiting for the results of the national meeting of bankers this week, traders said.
Total turnover fell sharply to 3.42 million lots from 7.24 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract ended unchanged at 11 percent.
Traders said institutions were unwilling to trade given the uncertainties over the results of the meeting.
"Rumours that the central bank will ban all commercial banks from trading on the T-bill repo market continued to support the seven-day contract," one local trader said.
Traders said the possible ban, if implemented, would cut money supply on the repo market, make trading less active and tend to push rates up.
The early-maturing contracts were also supported by the new issue of Baoding Swan Company Ltd on the Shenzhen stock market today, a second trader said.
But contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down due to the commercial bank ban rumour.
The most active three-year note that matures in 1999 rose slightly to 103 yuan from 102.93 yuan on Tuesday. Trading volume of the note fell sharply to 0.23 billion yuan from 0.70 billion.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market plunged to 594,910 lots from 1.43 million.
Traders said the bank ban rumour stopped the upward trend on the spots market with many long-term investors sidelined waiting for clear results of the national bankers meeting.
They said the results of the meeting would be a key factor in determining the short-term market direction.
